key_insight: Increasing the barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% produced denser detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings with better wear resistance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing detonation-spraying parameters can directly improve the durability of carbide-based protective coatings for high-friction, high-temperature components.
method: Prepared Cr3C2–NiCr coatings at 43% and 53% barrel filling ratios under identical detonation-spraying conditions.
Compared coating microstructure and phase composition using microscopy and XRD.
Evaluated dry sliding tribology with ball-on-disc tests at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% filling-ratio coating reached a minimum wear rate of 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N) and showed improved wear resistance at higher load despite a higher friction coefficient.
watch_item: The improved wear performance comes with a friction increase, so application-specific tradeoffs and operating loads should be checked before deployment.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
